text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Mubarak and U.S. Vice President Al Gore hold talks on encouraging investment and technology for Egypt and joint economic efforts between the two countries. Mubarak stresses to the heads of American banks and companies that all of his efforts are aimed at raising people's living standards and making jobs available.

- Senior Pentagon official tells al-Ahram that Mubarak and U.S. Defence Secretary William Cohen discussed regional developments in the Middle East, such as in Sudan, Libya, Iraq and Iran. The two agreed that security ties between their countries were good and must develop and strengthen, and there must be confidence-building measures between Israel and its Arab neighbours.

- Egypt and the United States will take part in the international meeting in Gaza on Saturday to discuss the challenges facing the peace process, responding to the invitation of Palestinian President Yasser Arafat.

- Mubarak says that there are American efforts to resume peace talks on the Syrian track and solve the problem of Abu Ghoneim. He tells the chief editors of Egyptian newspapers that bilateral cooperation with the United States is as good as it can be.
- Egyptian cabinet to discuss today a new legal regime governing ties between real estate owners and their tenants.
- Mubarak says that Egypt's ties with the United States are good despite some differences of opinion.
- Court sentences actors to one year prison and fines for taking part in a film which it said included shameful words and actions.
